children: Asian currencies consolidate against the dollar, but may be weighed by risk-off sentiment. These currencies could "remain on the defensive at the start of the week as elevated U.S. Treasury yields and renewed weakness in technology shares weigh on sentiment," OCBC Group Research strategists say in a note. "For the week ahead, we would watch whether foreign equity selling in Korea and Taiwan eases, alongside developments in oil prices, technology shares and U.S. Treasury yields," the strategists add. The U.S. dollar edges 0.1% lower to 1,333.90 won and is flat at 1.2879 Singapore dollars, while the Australian dollar is steady at US$0.6772, LSEG data show. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)
